draft.title: Independent events
card: Two events are independent if knowing that one happened does not change the probability of the other. Flipping a coin and rolling a die are independent.
For independent events A and B, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B). This means both happen.
Example: P(heads) = 1/2 and P(roll a 6) = 1/6. P(heads and a 6) = 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12.
To test for independence, check whether P(A ∩ B) equals P(A) × P(B). If it does, the events are independent. If it does not, they are not.
draft.remember: Independent events: multiply the probabilities to find P(A ∩ B).

a.q: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A ∩ B)?
a.why: For independent events, P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. Adding gives 0.9, which is the mistake of using the wrong operation and would not be a probability of both happening.
a.clue: Both events happen, and the events are independent.

b.q: For events A and B, P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.3. Which statement is correct?
opts: Not independent, as 0.3 is less than P(A)
b.why: Independent events need P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B). Here 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2, which is not 0.3, so the events are not independent. Being a valid probability between 0 and 1 does not test independence.
b.clue: Multiply P(A) and P(B), then compare with P(A ∩ B).
